triage_steps: Ask the customer to confirm if all devices are affected or only one.
Have the customer unplug the gateway power for 30 seconds and plug it back in.
Wait 5–10 minutes for lights to stabilize.
Run an equipment/connection test using internal tools or the app.
If the gateway is online but no internet, escalate to technician visit.
If an area outage is detected, inform the customer and share ETA.
Ask which apps or sites are affected and whether wired or WiFi connections are used.
Have the customer run a speed test using the Xfinity app or website.
Check for congestion patterns (peak evening hours).
Verify that the subscribed speed tier matches the customer's expectations.
Recommend optimizing WiFi placement or using wired connections where possible.
Ask if the issue happens on all channels or only specific ones.
Have the customer reboot the TV box and check cabling.
Check signal levels to the TV box using internal tools.
If signal issues persist, consider scheduling a technician visit.
If only specific channels are affected, check for channel-specific outages.
Ask the customer if they recently returned or swapped any equipment.
Verify which devices are currently listed on the account.
Check return records for recently returned equipment.
If a discrepancy is found, escalate to billing adjustment.
Explain that equipment fees apply when renting modems, gateways, or TV boxes.
Compare current bill to previous month to identify differences.
Check for promotional discounts that may have expired.
Check for one-time charges, overages, or new equipment.
Explain the main drivers of the change in simple terms.
If still unclear, escalate to billing specialist.
Confirm if the internet connection is stable.
Ask the customer to power cycle the camera and gateway.
Check if the device appears online in internal tools.
If the camera remains offline, schedule technician or device replacement.
For security issues, treat with higher priority if it's a complete outage.
